case_title: Edmunds Lyngdoh v. State of Meghalaya
statutory_provisions: IPC s. 420, 1208; Prevention of Corruption Act s. 5(2)
aggravating_circumstances: Abuse of position, pecuniary advantage, wrongful loss to NEHU
mitigating_circumstances: Age of accused, duration of pendency of matter, already paid fine and deposited amount
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 420 IPC, 1208 IPC and 5(2) of the PC Act
high_court_outcome: Enhanced sentence for first accused, reversed acquittal of accused 3 to 5
offence_finally_established: Criminal breach of trust, cheating, abuse of position
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the first accused, as Chief Engineer of NEHU, colluded with other officials to procure Damp Proof Cement (DPC) at an exorbitant rate from a dealer. The accused invited quotations from 12 firms, but only two were approved by the Purchase Committee. The DPC was purchased at Rs.42.75 per kg, while the market rate was between Rs.5 to Rs.10 per kg. The dealer quoted an inflated price to gain wrongful benefit and cause loss to NEHU. The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court upheld the conviction but modified the sentence for the fourth accused due to his age and the duration of the case. The fourth accused was sentenced to imprisonment for the conviction under Sections 420 IPC and 1208 IPC, with a fine imposed.
